case_name: Vinod Popli vs Ragini Popli & Ors
facts_of_case: Plaintiff seeks declaration and permanent injunction against wife, daughter, and son-in-law. He claims that memorandums of undertaking/compromise deed/undertaking are null and void. Plaintiff also seeks injunction restraining defendants from transferring or creating third-party rights in property.

legal_principles.principle: When parties to a legal controversy are in pari delicto, neither can obtain any relief from the Court since both are at equal fault or of equal guilt.
legal_principles.held: The principle of in pari delicto is clearly applicable to the present case.
cited_cases: Bateman Eichler, Hill Richards, Inc. v. Berner, 472 U.S. 299 (1985)

legal_principles.principle: A plaintiff who has participated in wrongdoing may not recover damages resulting from the wrongdoing.
legal_principles.held: The principle that a plaintiff who has participated in wrongdoing may not recover damages resulting from the wrongdoing is applicable to the present case.

outcome.final_order: The court declared the memorandums of undertaking/compromise deed/undertaking as null and void, and granted permanent injunction to the plaintiff.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for nullity of marriage
advising on property rights in divorce cases
preparing a response to an injunction application
